bookkeeping.title: Bookkeeping
bookkeeping.desc: Track all your sales, COGS, and operating expenses in one place. Your records are saved per account, so when you log in again you will find everything still here.

q1.title: What is monthly cash flow?
q1.body: Cash flow = cash received - cash paid. It shows if your business generated or lost cash in this month.

q2.title: Opening Cash:
q2.body: This is the amount of cash you already have at the start of the month — usually the closing cash from the previous month.

q3.title: Closing Cash:
q3.body: The closing cash shows how much money your business has left at the end of the month — after all inflows and outflows are accounted for.

q4.title: Total Inflows:
q4.body: This represents all the actual cash your business received during the month — like cash from sales, investor funding, or any other money that physically entered your account or cash box.

q5.title: Total Outflows:
q5.body: This represents all the actual cash your business paid out during the month — such as product costs, salaries, marketing, rent, or any expense that was truly paid in cash or deducted from your bank balance.

q6.title: Important:
q6.body: These numbers only track real cash movement — the actual money that went in and out during this month.

q7.title: How to use:
q7.body: Enter all inflows (sales, other income) and outflows (COGS, salaries, marketing, taxes, owner pay). This calculator gives your net and closing cash instantly.

incomeStatementPage.flow: Flow: Sales Revenue → COGS → Gross Profit → OPEX → Net Profit → Owner's Withdrawals → Retained Profit.

explain.drawingsBody: the money that the owner takes from the Net Profit for personal use. It's not a business expense, it's simply money taken out of the company by the owner.
explain.retainedBody: the money reinvested in the business after the owner takes their withdrawals. It stays in the company to help it grow, expand production, or fund new collections.

target.marginNote: (the percentage of your final selling price that is your profit)

packagingCostBuilderPage.title: RunwayToRevenue – Packaging Cost Builder

currency.label: Currency
currency.hint: Use the same currency you use in your pricing & manufacturing tools.

packagingCostBuilderPage.subtitle: Build your full packaging cost per order and per item. Plug this into your pricing calculator so you don't underestimate COGS.

items.label: Average items per order
items.note: For example: many brands average 1–3 items per order.

orders.label: Orders per month (optional)
orders.note: We'll show your total monthly packaging spend using this.

outerBox.label: Outer mailer / box – cost per order
outerBox.note: Custom mailer, shipping box or polymailer used once per order.

polybag.label: Inner poly bag – cost per item
polybag.note: Cost for one product bag. We multiply by items per order.

extraPack.label: Extra / custom packaging – per order
extraPack.note: Ribbons, dust bags, special boxes, limited drop extras, etc.

labour.title: Fulfilment labour
labour.note: Example: if it takes 5 minutes to pack and the packer is paid 60 per hour, labour cost per order ≈ (5 ÷ 60) × 60 = 5.

explain.title: How this model works:
explain.step1: 1) We build your material cost per order from the outer mailer, poly bags, tissue, inserts, stickers, labels, tape and any extras.
explain.step2: 2) We convert your packing time and hourly wage into a labour cost per order.
explain.step3: 3) We add them together to get total packaging cost per order and divide by your average items per order to get packaging cost per item.

how.title: How to use this with your other tools:
how.step1: • Take the packaging cost per item and add it into your Manufacturing Cost Tool or directly into your Pricing Calculator as part of COGS.
how.step2: • If you upgrade your packaging (new box, dust bag, thank-you kit), update these numbers so your prices always match your real costs.

manufacturerCostPage.subtitle: Use this before you send money to a factory. Enter the quantity, per-unit costs (fabric, cut & sew, prints, trims, packaging) and order-level costs (shipping, duty, other). The tool will give you your real all-in cost per unit and total order cost.

perUnit.title: Per-unit production costs
perUnit.note: These are costs you pay per piece. If you double units, this part roughly doubles.
perUnit.explain: Cut & sew = labour the factory charges to turn fabric into a finished garment (cutting panels, stitching, assembling). Trims & labels = physical extras like woven neck labels, hem tags, hang tags, patches, etc. If your factory gives you one combined price like "cut, make & trim", you can put that full number in either Cut & sew or Trims & labels and leave the other at 0.

orderLevel.title: Order-level costs
orderLevel.note: These are one-time costs for the whole order, not per piece.
orderLevel.examples: Examples: freight, customs, port fees, bank transfer fees, QC inspection, etc.

summary.title: Cost Summary
summary.note: Numbers below update automatically as you type. Currency is shown as {symbol} by default – just think in the same currency you use in your pricing and income statement tools.
summary.allInNote: All-in cost per unit = (total per-unit costs × units + all order-level costs) ÷ units. Use this number inside your pricing calculator.
summary.basePerUnit: Base per-unit costs (fabric, cut & sew, etc.)
summary.overheadPerUnit: Order overhead per unit (shipping, duty, other ÷ units)
summary.breakdownNote: Base per-unit + overhead per-unit = all-in cost per unit. If you raise or lower your quantity, overhead per unit will change a lot.

productionPlannerPage.subtitle: Plan your next drop based on MOQ, demand, and budget. This tool shows you your recommended units, total cost, conflicts, and what is driving the recommendation.

currency.label: Currency
currency.hint: Use the same currency you use in your pricing & manufacturing tools.

unitCost.label: Unit cost (all-in per piece)

explain.title: How the recommendation works:

returnsExchangePage.title: RunwayToRevenue – Returns / Exchange Cost Model
returnsExchangePage.subtitle: This model shows how returns and exchanges eat into your profit. It calculates the extra cost per order and for a full month, based on your return rate, exchange rate and handling costs.

currency.label: Currency
currency.hint: Use the same currency you use in your pricing & income statement tools.

aov.label: Average Order Value (AOV)
aov.note: The average amount a customer pays for one order.

cogs.label: Product + Fulfilment Cost per Order
cogs.note: All non-ad costs to deliver one order: product, packaging, shipping to customer, etc.

other.label: Other Variable Cost per Order
other.note: Payment fees, platform fees, per-order apps, etc.

orders.label: Orders per Month
orders.note: How many orders you expect this month. We use this to show the total monthly impact of returns & exchanges.

rates.title: Return & Exchange Rates
rates.returnNote: Percentage of all orders that are returned (sale is at risk).
rates.exchangeNote: Percentage of all orders that become exchanges (customer keeps buying, but you pay extra shipping/handling).

costReturn.title: Cost per Return
costReturn.note: Value lost can be discounts, damaged pieces, or stock you can’t resell.

explain.title: How this model works:
explain.step1: 1) We first calculate your base profit per order = AOV - (product + fulfilment + other variable costs).
explain.step2: 2) Then we add the expected cost of returns & exchanges per order, based on your return rate, exchange rate and handling costs.
explain.step3: 3) Finally we show your profit after returns/exchanges per order and the total monthly impact.

results.title: Results
results.extraPerOrder: Extra expected cost per order from returns & exchanges
results.profitAfter: Profit per order after returns & exchanges
results.monthlyExtra: Extra monthly cost from returns & exchanges
results.tip: Tip: combine this with your ROAS / CPA Break-Even Calculator and Manufacturing Cost Tool to see the full picture: product cost ? returns & exchanges ? ads ? final profit.

roasCpaPage.title: RunwayToRevenue – ROAS / CPA Break-Even Calculator
roasCpaPage.subtitle: This tool shows your break-even CPA and break-even ROAS, then compares them with your actual CPA and ROAS. Use the same inputs you use in your pricing calculator: average order value, cost per order, and ad spend per order.

currency.label: Currency
currency.hint: Use the same currency you use in your pricing & income statement tools.

aov.label: Average Order Value (AOV)
aov.note: The average amount a customer pays for one order.

cogs.label: Product + Fulfilment Cost per Order
cogs.note: All costs to deliver one order: product, packaging, shipping to customer, etc.

other.label: Other Variable Cost per Order
other.note: Payment fees, platform fees, per-order app fees, etc.

target.label: Target Profit Margin % (optional)
target.note: The % of revenue you want as profit after ads. Example: 20%.

cpa.label: CPA (Cost per Attribute)
cpa.note: In this calculator, the attribute = purchase. So this CPA is how much you pay in ads to get one order (total ad spend ÷ number of purchases).

explain.p1: What does “profit before ads” mean? It’s your revenue per order minus all non-ad costs (product, packaging, shipping-to-customer, payment fees, etc.). Basically: “If I spent zero on ads, how much profit would I make from one order?”
explain.p2: ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) = Revenue ÷ Ad Spend. Here we look at it per order as AOV ÷ CPA, where CPA (cost per attribute) is the ad cost for one purchase (one completed order).
explain.p3: Break-even CPA is your profit before ads per order. If your real CPA is lower than this, you still keep profit. If it’s higher, you lose money on each order.
explain.p4: Example: AOV = 1000, non-ad costs = 500 ? profit before ads = 500 (this is your break-even CPA). If CPA = 300 ? profit after ads = 200 (good). If CPA = 500 ? break-even. If CPA = 700 ? you lose 200 per order.

results.title: Results
results.tip: Tip: Get your real cost per order from the Manufacturing Cost Tool + shipping-to-customer and payment fees. Then test different CPAs and see how aggressive you can be with ads while keeping healthy profit.

status.enterCpa: Enter a CPA to compare with your target margin.

roasCalculatorPage.title: RunwayToRevenue – ROAS / CPA Break-Even Calculator
roasCalculatorPage.subtitle: This tool shows your break-even CPA and break-even ROAS, then compares them with your actual CPA and ROAS. Use the same inputs you use in your pricing calculator: average order value, cost per order, and ad spend per order.

currency.label: Currency
currency.hint: Use the same currency you use in your pricing & income statement tools.

aov.label: Average Order Value (AOV)
aov.note: The average amount a customer pays for one order.

cogs.label: Product + Fulfilment Cost per Order
cogs.note: All costs to deliver one order: product, packaging, shipping to customer, etc.

other.label: Other Variable Cost per Order
other.note: Payment fees, platform fees, per-order app fees, etc.

target.label: Target Profit Margin % (optional)
target.note: The % of revenue you want as profit after ads. Example: 20%.

cpa.label: CPA (Cost per Attribute)
cpa.note: In this calculator, the attribute = purchase. So this CPA is how much you pay in ads to get one order (total ad spend ÷ number of purchases).

explain.p1: What does “profit before ads” mean? It’s your revenue per order minus all non-ad costs (product, packaging, shipping-to-customer, payment fees, etc.). Basically: “If I spent zero on ads, how much profit would I make from one order?”
explain.p2: ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) = Revenue ÷ Ad Spend. Here we look at it per order as AOV ÷ CPA, where CPA (cost per attribute) is the ad cost for one purchase (one completed order).
explain.p3: Break-even CPA is your profit before ads per order. If your real CPA is lower than this, you still keep profit. If it’s higher, you lose money on each order.
explain.p4: Example: AOV = 1000, non-ad costs = 500 ? profit before ads = 500 (this is your break-even CPA). If CPA = 300 ? profit after ads = 200 (good). If CPA = 500 ? break-even. If CPA = 700 ? you lose 200 per order.

results.title: Results
results.tip: Tip: Get your real cost per order from the Manufacturing Cost Tool + shipping-to-customer and payment fees. Then test different CPAs and see how aggressive you can be with ads while keeping healthy profit.
